Add diagnosis prefix flags

Source: R/open-flags.R
nis_flag_dx.Rd

Each diagnosis slot is checked separately. Supplied prefixes are case-insensitive, and periods and spaces in them are ignored. Slot values are compared as stored, case sensitively, because NIS stores upper-case codes without periods. Matching stays lazy in DuckDB and avoids per-row text normalization.

Usage

nis_flag_dx(
  .data,
  ...,
  position = c("any", "principal", "secondary"),
  system = c("icd10", "icd9")
)

Arguments

.data

A data frame or lazy DuckDB query.

...

Named flag definitions, such as heart_failure = "I50".

position

Slots to check: all slots, the principal slot, or secondary slots only.

system

Code system of the slots to check: "icd10" (default) or "icd9" (experimental, NIS 2012 to Q3 2015).

Value

.data with one logical column per named definition.

Details

system picks which slots are tested. "icd10" reads I10_DX1, I10_DX2, ...; "icd9" (experimental) reads DX1, DX2, ... as stored in NIS 2012 through Q3 2015. A prefix is only ever compared with slots of the chosen system, so an ICD-10 flag never matches an ICD-9 slot and the reverse.

In 2015 the Q1-Q3 discharges carry ICD-9 codes and the Q4 discharges carry ICD-10 codes. HCUP is understood to recommend DXVER (9 or 10) to distinguish them, because DQTR can be missing (UNVERIFIED: secondhand); PRVER describes the procedure system. Non-missing version indicators must agree with system; non-missing YEAR and, in 2015, DQTR must also agree. Conflicting or invalid indicators yield FALSE. Missing indicators rely on the slot namespace: callers must preserve the official names and leave inapplicable slots missing. Shared slots containing both systems are not supported. FALSE means "not flagged under that code system", not "condition absent". A study that crosses October 2015 needs analyst-supplied code sets for both systems, flagged in two calls and combined, for example nis_flag_dx(hf10 = "I50") |> nis_flag_dx(hf9 = "428", system = "icd9") |> dplyr::mutate(hf = hf10 | hf9). easyNIS ships no code lists and no ICD-9 to ICD-10 crosswalk, and even with both code sets, counts of a condition can break at the transition.

Examples

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020))
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpLVUyQx/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpLVUyQx/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpLVUyQx/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
nis |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50") |>
  dplyr::count(heart_failure) |>
  dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   heart_failure     n
#>   <lgl>         <dbl>
#> 1 FALSE            84
#> 2 TRUE            108

# Several prefixes, restricted to the principal diagnosis
nis |>
  nis_flag_dx(hf_or_diabetes = c("I50", "E11"), position = "principal") |>
  dplyr::count(hf_or_diabetes) |>
  dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   hf_or_diabetes     n
#>   <lgl>          <dbl>
#> 1 FALSE             84
#> 2 TRUE             108
